I think the most important tasks include 

- [ ] github app installation webhook 
- [x] versioning #177 
- [ ] auto updates #116 

@sepo-agent /answer 
what do you think?

comments.body:
I agree these are the right top priorities, but I’d order them slightly differently:

1. **Versioning / release identity first (#177)**
   This blocks the other two. Right now `.agent/package.json` says `0.1.0`, while `.agent/sepo-version.json` also says `0.1.0` but still points at `main` with `source_sha: null`:  
   https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/package.json#L2-L4  
   https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/sepo-version.json#L2-L9

   Before a formal `v0.1.0`, we should decide the source of truth: package version in `.agent/package.json`, and optional install provenance separately. Then tag/release `v0.1.0` from that.

2. **Auto updates second (#116)**
   #116 looks close and useful, but for release readiness I would not default updates to moving `main`. The versioning docs already say release installs should use tags like `v0.1.0`:  
   https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/docs/technical-details/versioning.md#L7-L13

   So #116 should ideally resolve latest release/tag and open PRs like “Update Sepo from v0.1.0 to v0.1.1”, with file diff as validation.

3. **GitHub App installation webhook third**
   Important, but the real implementation belongs in the hosted GitHub App backend: receive `installation` events, verify signature, mint installation token, dispatch `agent-onboarding.yml`, or create/update a setup issue fallback. The repo already has the onboarding workflow/manual path:  
   https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/workflows/agent-onboarding.yml#L1-L69

   I would avoid treating repo-local `installation-bootstrap.ts` as the core solution unless the hosted backend actually imports a built Sepo package. The backend should implement the dispatch/fallback behavior directly.

One extra release gate I’d add: a clean install smoke test. Before tagging `v0.1.0`, install Sepo into a fresh repo, run onboarding, try `/answer`, and verify the update check can see the current installed version.

So my recommended pre-`v0.1.0` checklist is:

- [ ] Resolve #177: one canonical version source plus clear install provenance.
- [ ] Tag/release `v0.1.0` from `main`.
- [ ] Adjust/merge #116 so updates target release tags, not `main`.
- [ ] Implement hosted GitHub App installation webhook behavior, with manual onboarding fallback.
- [ ] Run a fresh-repo install/onboarding/update smoke test.

title: Most high priority tasks before a formal v0.1.0 release
